title: Gas barbecue grill: safe teardown
summary: A propane grill gives a cylinder of propane, a spark igniter, a lid thermometer, cooking grates, stainless burners and a steel cart. Close the cylinder valve and take the cylinder well away before anything else. Leave the regulator, hose, valves and manifold on the grill: never open a gas joint or reuse those parts on anything else.

steps.text: Work outdoors in the open, with the grill cold (Dyna-Glo says about 45 minutes after use) and every burner out. Before you touch anything, sniff near the knobs, the hose and the cylinder, but don't trust your nose alone: the smell added to propane can fade.
steps.warn: If you smell gas: no flame, spark, phone or switch nearby. Close the cylinder valve if you can reach it safely, open the lid and move away; if the smell stays, keep away (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual). Propane sinks and pools in low spots.

steps.text: Turn every burner knob to OFF. Then close the cylinder valve: turn its handwheel clockwise to a full stop (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual).
steps.warn: Don't force a seized valve with a tool. If it won't close, keep everyone and any flame away from the grill and cylinder, and don't carry them indoors.

steps.text: If the grill is piped to a building's gas line instead of a cylinder, skip steps 4 and 5 and close the shut-off valve on that line and have the grill disconnected and the line capped by someone able to do gas work. Until then, leave every gas part alone and take only the grates, thermometer and igniter battery.
steps.warn: Never leave an open gas pipe, and never plug one with tape, a bung or a hose.

steps.text: Take the regulator off the cylinder: turn the large coupling nut anticlockwise by hand until it comes free: both makers' manuals give anticlockwise for their large coupling nut (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual, Nexgrill 720-0830H manual). CPSC's fact sheet describes a connector that comes off turning clockwise, so if the nut won't turn, check which style you have and never force it. Dyna-Glo has it done up by hand only, without tools (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual). Fit the cylinder's own dust cap onto its valve outlet (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual, Nexgrill 720-0830H manual).
steps.warn: Use only the cap that came with that valve; a different cap or plug may not seal (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual). A little gas can escape as the nut comes off: do this outdoors, with no flame or spark near.

steps.text: Undo the screw or bolt that holds the cylinder in the cart (the Dyna-Glo parts list has a cylinder retention screw, the Nexgrill a tank bolt). Carry the cylinder upright, by its collar, well away from the grill and from where you will work, and stand it upright outdoors (CPSC Publication 467), out of the sun: Dyna-Glo says never where it can reach 52 °C (125 °F). Look it over: Nexgrill says never to use a dented or rusty cylinder (Nexgrill 720-0830H manual). Leave a bulging or fire-damaged one too.
steps.warn: Never store or use a cylinder indoors, in a garage or shed, or anywhere it can pass 52 °C (125 °F), such as a hot car (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual, CPSC Publication 467). Don't drop it or knock the valve.

steps.text: Lift out the cooking grates, then the heat tents or flavour bars, the warming rack and the grease tray. Wear gloves: old grill steel is often rusty and sharp-edged, and porcelain enamel chips.

Take out the igniter battery. On the Dyna-Glo, unscrew the igniter cap and pull the AA cell out of the igniter body (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual). Weber's parts schematic lists the ignition module, button and electrode wires as separate parts (Weber 45010001); how they are fixed varies by grill, so look before you pull.
Undo the thermometer's nut and pull the thermometer out of the lid; the Dyna-Glo's is held by a nut (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual).

If the grill still works, keep it as an outdoor cooker and go no further: put the parts back. Look over the hose and regulator first, and if the hose is cracked, cut or worn, don't use the grill (CPSC Publication 467, Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual). Each time you connect a cylinder, leak-test every connection with soapy water before you light it.

Retired grill only: take out the burners. Nexgrill: pull the pin at the back of each burner and the screw at the front, then lift the burner off its gas valve's orifice (Nexgrill 720-0830H manual). Dyna-Glo: pull the hinge pin, undo the two screws that hold the igniter electrode to the burner, and slide the burner out of the firebox (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual).
steps.warn: Leave the orifices, valves, manifold, hose, regulator and any side-burner gas line where they are. Never undo a gas joint, and never take a valve or regulator off to use as a gas part.

steps.text: Before you undo the cart panels or casters, have a helper hold the firebox or rest it on blocks: it sits on the cart, and Dyna-Glo says its grill is heavy and takes two people to assemble. Then take the side shelves, cart panels and doors, the door magnets, the casters or wheels with their axle, and any tank scale (Nexgrill 720-0830H manual, Weber 45010001).
Leave the firebox and control panel with the gas parts still fixed to them. Tie a tag on the grill: "Gas parts. Do not connect to gas or light."

notes:
## Gas first

- **If you smell gas,** the makers say to shut off the gas, put out any flame and open the lid, and if the smell stays, to keep away and call the gas supplier or fire department (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual, Nexgrill 720-0830H manual). With nobody to call, keep away and let it air.
- **Leak test.** With every knob off and the cylinder valve open, brush or spray soapy water on each connection: CPSC uses one part liquid detergent to one part water, Dyna-Glo one part dish soap to three parts water. Bubbles mean a leak. Close the cylinder valve and tighten the joint, by hand only on the cylinder coupling nut (Dyna-Glo and Nexgrill both say no tools, and Nexgrill says a wrench can damage the nut and make a hazard); if it still leaks, close the valve and don't use the grill (CPSC Publication 467, Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual). At the cylinder joint, Weber has you close the tank valve, take the regulator off, check the tank valve gasket and refit it, then try a second tank if it still leaks (Weber tank connection). Never look for leaks with a flame (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual).
- **The gas parts stay put.** The makers say to use only the regulator and hose supplied with the grill, and never to connect a cylinder without a regulator (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual, Nexgrill 720-0830H manual). A burner must sit centred on its orifice or a fire or explosion can follow, and Nexgrill advises a trained technician to replace one (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual, Nexgrill 720-0830H manual). So the regulator, hose, valves and burners are not spares for home-made stoves or lamps.
- **Spiders.** Insects and spiders nest in the burner tubes, and a blocked tube can start a fire under the grill. Check them at least once a year and push any blockage through with a pipe cleaner or wire (CPSC Publication 467, Nexgrill 720-0830H manual).
- **Carbon monoxide.** Grills are for outdoors only: never in a garage, shed, porch or other enclosed space (Nexgrill 720-0830H manual). See safety_carbon_monoxide.

## What's worth keeping and why

- **The whole grill, if it works.** A ready-made outdoor cooker. The Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D is rated 36,000 BTU/h, about 10.5 kW (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual).
- **Propane and the cylinder.** The 20 lb cylinder holds about 9 kg (20 lb) of propane when full. It must carry a listed overfill prevention device and a collar to guard the valve, and is never filled past 80 % (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual). Nexgrill says to have it filled by a propane dealer and inspected and requalified at each filling (Nexgrill 720-0830H manual). Weigh it against an empty one to judge what's left. Connect it only to an appliance whose maker allows a 20 lb cylinder, using that appliance's own regulator and hose, and leak-test as above. CPSC says never to fill a cylinder yourself. Keep it upright and outdoors, out of the sun, and never store a spare under or near a grill (CPSC Publication 467). It must stand upright so it gives off vapour, not liquid (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual).
- **Igniter.** The Dyna-Glo has an electronic ignition housing, an electrode and wire assembly and a heat shield, and runs on one AA cell (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual). Weber lists an ignition module, a button and electrode wires as separate parts (Weber 45010001). With a fresh battery it gives a spark to light a gas burner made for it.
- **Thermometer.** The Dyna-Glo lists a temperature gauge with nut, part 104-12005 (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual); the Nexgrill lists a gauge and its housing as separate parts (Nexgrill 720-0830H manual). Use it on a solar oven or smoker (build_solar_oven).
- **Grates.** The Dyna-Glo's are porcelain-enamelled and chip if knocked (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual). Cook on them over a wood fire.
- **Burners, flame tamers and flavour bars.** The Dyna-Glo burners and the Nexgrill flame tamers are stainless steel; Weber's Flavorizer bars are porcelain-enamelled (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual, Nexgrill 720-0830H manual, Weber 45010001). Use them as steel tube and sheet only.
- **Cart parts.** Casters, wheels and an axle, door magnets, steel panels and shelves (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual, Nexgrill 720-0830H manual, Weber 45010001).

## Variations

- **Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D:** 3 burners, 36,000 BTU/h, AA electronic ignition. Its firebox assembly is sold with the burners, valves and manifold, hose and regulator and control panel as one part (Dyna-Glo DGB390SNP-D manual).
- **Nexgrill 720-0830H:** 4 main burners of 12,000 BTU/h each plus a 12,000 BTU/h side burner, 60,000 BTU/h in all; a pulse igniter module, the igniter built into each valve, and a flexible gas line to the side burner (Nexgrill 720-0830H manual).
- **Weber Spirit II E-310 LP:** 3 burners; parts list an igniter kit, a hose and regulator kit, an LP manifold, a burner tube kit, a crossover tube, a heat deflector (SS), a corrugated gas line and a tank scale (Weber 45010001).
- **Natural gas:** some grills are piped to the building. Nexgrill says its propane grill must not be run on natural gas unless it has been converted (Nexgrill 720-0830H manual).

## What to leave

- **Every gas part:** regulator and hose, manifold, valves, orifices and any side-burner gas line.
- **A dented, rusty, bulging or burnt cylinder.**
- **Plastic knobs and shelf trims,** unless you need them.

## Testing what you got out

- **Cylinder and connections:** the soapy-water test above, every time you connect.
- **Igniter:** fit a fresh battery, press the button and look for a spark at the electrode. Keep fingers off the tip.
- **Thermometer:** in boiling water it should read close to 100 °C (212 °F) near sea level, a little less higher up.
